name: South-east gate ("sluice gate")
period: late 3rd century AD (c. 270–280): the stone wall as newly built, all gates open
conventions: u along the town wall, v out to the field (so the "n" drawing is the field front); metres; origin the anchor corner

rooms.name: Footway
rooms.note: Fulford's re-excavation (1976) read the "sluice gate" as a pedestrian gate with a drain beneath (C&F 2016)

walls.note: masonry passage wall with brick piers (the stepped outline in the GIS) holding back the rampart; the passage began in timber, then timber with masonry infill, then brick piers and masonry (C&F 2016, after Fulford 1984)

openings.note: the footway's outer ring, carried up as the parapet (conjecture)
footway about 1.2 m wide through the wall, with a drain beneath (C&F 2016); later blocked (the GIS strip across its inner end): shown open

platforms.note: the wall-walk carried over the footway

drawings.caption: Field front: the footway through the wall
Section along the footway: the passage walls holding back the rampart, the arch through the wall
